text:
zoe (Product): Putting a stake in the ground for the Playground streaming UX. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/stream-ux. Key decisions: how tokens visually arrive (append vs shimmer), what the primary action should read (Stop / Interrupt / Cancel), where the token counter lives during stream, and whether prompt library should be editable mid-run. Quick takes?

matt (Frontend): New idea: instead of full shimmer, use an "append buffer" area that layers incoming chunks and crossfades them into the main thread when finalized. Minimizes jank and keeps focus stable.

priya (Eng): Append buffer is great. Backend-wise we stream partial chunks and have a finalize event. On interrupt we cancel; no resume. So button should indicate that finality.

ella (A11y): If we go append buffer, ensure each finalized chunk is announced via aria-live="polite" and group small chunks to avoid chattiness. Also the token counter needs an accessible label and a visible focus target.

cam (PM): On wording: customers confuse Stop vs Cancel. "Interrupt" is precise but a bit technical. How about "Stop generation" as the visible label and a tooltip that explains partial results?

zoe (Product): I like "Stop generation" + tooltip: "Stops generation. Partial response may be returned. Regenerate to retry." Keeps label friendly. Also we should add a keyboard shortcut (I) to interrupt for power users.

matt (Frontend): Keyboard shortcut good call. We'll expose focusable stop button and add a small hint in the tooltip: "Shortcut: I". For the token counter I propose a compact floating pill on the right rail showing current tokens and a small delta indicator "+N" when interrupt changes counts.

priya (Eng): The "+N" delta is interesting. It can show if post-processing increases/decreases tokens after interrupt. We'll emit a summary update after finalize that the frontend can animate into the pill.

ella (A11y): For that delta, surface it visually and also as text for screen readers: e.g., "Token count updated to 412 (changed by +12)" announced via aria-live once. Coalesce with other announcements.

cam (PM): Prompt library behavior: users want to browse while a run is active but not accidentally apply templates. Proposal: keep library interactive but disable the primary "Apply" action with caption "Applies to next run" and make it keyboard-focusable with aria-disabled. If user selects a template and then hits Regenerate after stopping, show a confirmation toast: "Using selected template for next run."

zoe (Product): UX detail: when a prompt is selected mid-stream, show a subtle stacked badge in the right rail that says "Pending: <template name>" so users know it's queued. Badge disappears after next generation.

matt (Frontend): I'll add that pending badge. Also debounce token updates to 200ms and animate the delta on update with a short color flash so users notice the change after interrupt.

priya (Eng): Edge-case: interrupt may trigger fallback model which encodes tokens differently. We'll include a microcopy inside pill tooltip: "Counts are approximate during streaming and may change after stop."

ella (A11y): Make sure the stop button is first in tab order and the pending badge is reachable. Disabled Apply buttons must have aria-describedby that points to the "Applies to next run" note.

cam (PM): Action items: matt prototype append-buffer + token pill + pending badge by Wed, ella to review a11y strings after prototype, priya to confirm cancel semantics with infra, zoe to update Figma microcopy. deploy-bot: schedule staging?

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled for branch playground/append-counter -> staging at 2026-05-14 01:00 UTC

zoe (Product): Thanks all. If prototype passes a11y review we'll ship and iterate on microcopy after user tests.
